questionnaire.title: FortKnight startup questionnaire
notes: Question definitions and slider bounds for the questionnaire (docs/questionnaire.md). The app renders from this file; answers become a weights file via fk_core/weights.py (Python) or app/shared/weights-rules.js (JavaScript).
Slider bounds are integer minutes per day, transcribed from the draft's hours; the 'more' checkbox raises the ceiling to moreMax (twice the normal ceiling, capped at a day).

Block split: the unscheduled block (start + length) sets the waking window; categories whose share is at least standoutMultiplier x the mean non-peripheral share each earn a focus block (capped at maxFocusBlocks; none -> one flexible block); Agenda scope 'categories' (the default) adds one more focus block, still capped; cuts start from an even split and snap to a cutGridMinutes grid within +/- cutSearchMinutes, preferring the edges of fixed activities (edgeBonus) and avoiding straddling them (straddlePenalty, soft).

Typical-person defaults: each subject opens at its `default` range with `peripheralByDefault` deciding the 'not often' box; `defaultAnswers` pre-ticks category boxes so the form can be submitted untouched.

Goal toggle: a subject marked `goal` is something the person wants in the schedule but does not do yet at that level; the form asks for the current actual (`currentMinutesPerDay`). A category with any goal subject counts as `wantMore` (x wantMoreMultiplier). Shares still use the goal range; the generator can ramp from current to goal.

Rhythm & appointments: meals (count + time-of-day slots), year split (scheme + sections), standing appointments and tasks (weekdays + plain-language cadence; appointments become anchors alongside fixed activities and vote for their category's preferredBlocks; tasks are placed by a time-of-day word, never anchors), preferred appointment weekdays, and practices are recorded on the weights file for the generator. Startup Q2 lists the person's commitments (standing appointments) and tasks by hand; an import document (data/schema/import.schema.json, version 2 written for the person to read) is applied on the Assistant page: its commitments/standing appointments are appended to the standingAppointments answer, its tasks reach the day pages, its fixed activities become anchors and its block focus grid becomes the profile's blockFocusGrid (FortKnight's Overview); the default paste is FortKnight's empty example (build/derived/defaultImport.json); a person's own document — such as the workbook example set's (examples/workbook) — replaces it.

Year split: any scheme prefills an editable section table (title, type, Gregorian equivalent, duration in weeks, start markers: date, rule, holiday, weather, manual); the result is the person's own year — the generator will later turn it into seasons like data/seasons.json.

Agenda context (no share effect, recorded on the weights file for an assistant or generator): rest days (`restDays`), the person's energy peak (`energyPeak`), and free-text `context`. Section order is Startup, Your day and year, Your week, Focus, About you (FortKnight's questionnaire), then Your meals (face 'forkknife': ForkKnife's questionnaire — the meals question plus meal preferences the ForkKnife assistant page's prompt embeds); a section's optional `face` (default 'fortknight') says which questionnaire page renders it; the app renders sections and questions in file order.

questions.prompt: How many people are in your group?
questions.note: Groups stay on one device for now — one profile per person.

questions.prompt: Do you already use a calendar, task list, reminder and/or budget system?
questions.note: Add them one at a time below. Commitments are timed — appointments, lessons, work or school hours — and become the anchors your day's blocks are cut around. Tasks have a day but no clock time, like chores and errands, and show on your day pages. Or have your assistant read your existing system and upload its import on the Assistant page; what it brought in shows here.

sections.title: Your day and year
sections.intro: The rest of the questions have preset defaults; change them now or later on this page. First the shape of a day and of a year: everything inside your waking window is the agenda's scope. Your meals — names, prepping and cooking, when you eat them and the fortnight menu — are ForkKnife's questionnaire.

questions.prompt: When are you awake?
questions.note: Drag both ends — from waking up to winding down, 10–18 hours; the end may pass midnight. Outside it is your unscheduled block (wind-down, sleep, wake-up); inside it is cut into 1–4 focus blocks by your Focus answers.

questions.prompt: On which day of the week do you start your week?
questions.note: The day your fortnight restarts on: sections snap to it by default, every section starts on that weekday (week A or B), and the fortnight grid begins with it.

questions.prompt: How do you like to split your year?
What weekday(s) do you like to schedule appointments on?
questions.note: Leave empty for any day.

questions.prompt: Which weekdays are your days off?
questions.note: Rest days carry no work-type commitments; an assistant building your agenda keeps them lighter. Leave empty when every day is alike.

sections.title: Focus
sections.intro: How the waking window is divided between the categories, and how many focus blocks a day earns.

questions.prompt: How long can you spend on each in a single day?
questions.note: Slide the bar for each subject to set a time range. Mark a subject "not often" to keep it out of your agenda; a few peripheral ones may still appear, marked as such. Tick "goal" on anything you want in the schedule but do not do at that level yet, and say where you are today. A category with a goal in it gets extra weight.

questions.prompt: Mark which categories you struggle with, and which you enjoy.
questions.note: Do not mark any subjects you have a neutral relationship with.

questions.prompt: Which categories can you easily hand off to someone else? (delegate, defer, pause, pay for, take a sabbatical from, etc.)
questions.intro: During an active emergency (sick days, out of town, etc.), a grieving or transition period, a time of struggle (health, financial, emotional, etc.), crunch time, or recovery:

questions.prompt: Mark 1–3 categories you have to do personally, even under duress.
Mark which of the following practices you participate in or would like to participate in:
questions.note: Used for planning suggestions; it does not change your shares yet.

questions.prompt: Do you want your day to include subjects or just categories?
questions.note: Categories adds one wide-scope focus block to your day beside the blocks your standout categories earn (the default day is early, midday, late). Subjects keeps only the earned blocks; when nothing stands out, that is a single flexible block.

sections.title: About you
sections.intro: Context an assistant needs to turn the answers above into an actual agenda; nothing here changes shares.

questions.prompt: When in the day are you sharpest?
questions.note: Tells an assistant which block should carry your demanding focus (deep work, study, hard chores) and which carries the light ones. It does not change shares.

questions.prompt: Anything an assistant should know when building your agenda?
questions.note: Household and care duties, shift patterns, commutes, recovery or a season of life, what should alternate between week A and week B, anything the sliders cannot say. Kept with your answers and shared only through the workspace files you download.
questions.placeholder: e.g. Two kids at school 08:30-15:00; I work from home Mon-Wed and on site Thu-Fri; deep cleaning every other Saturday (week B).

sections.title: Your meals
sections.intro: ForkKnife's questionnaire: your meals and what your assistant needs to draft the fortnight menu. Nothing here changes FortKnight's shares; the meals and their prep and cooking minutes reach the generator, everything else travels with your answers to your assistant workspace.

questions.prompt: What are your meals, and does each need prepping or cooking?
questions.note: Between 2 and 5 meals. Name each, tick when you eat it (one or two times of day), and say whether a menu item of that meal needs prepping, cooking, or both — the sliders are how long that takes. Snacks usually only need prepping. Renaming a meal keeps its dishes; dropping a meal drops them.

questions.prompt: How many people eat these meals with you (including you)?
questions.note: Portions and leftovers are planned for this many.

questions.prompt: Which dietary rules apply to the menu?
questions.note: Tick all that apply; leave blank for no rule.

questions.prompt: Allergies, intolerances, foods you won't eat?
questions.note: Free text; your assistant keeps them out of the menu.
questions.placeholder: e.g. shellfish allergy; no mushrooms; lactose only in small amounts.

questions.prompt: Which cuisines do you like most?
questions.note: Tick a few; the menu leans on them.

questions.prompt: Dishes you already cook and like?
questions.note: The assistant keeps them in the rotation.
questions.placeholder: e.g. lentil soup, tacos, roast chicken, overnight oats.

questions.prompt: How would you rate your cooking?
What is your food budget like?
What is in your kitchen?
questions.note: Tick what the menu may rely on.

questions.prompt: How often do you shop for food?
questions.note: Sets how fresh the ingredients can be and how far ahead the menu is bought.

byBlockFocus.method: Each early/midday/late block gives its full duration to its focus; flexible blocks are counted as 'flexible'.

byActivities.method: Timed activities count duration + prep minutes; untimed activities split the block's remaining minutes evenly; multi-category activities split evenly across categories.

source.description: FortKnight's empty example — replace it with the import document your assistant wrote from your calendar, planner or task list (docs/importers.md)

review: This is the shape, not your schedule: `commitments` are timed things (appointments, lessons, work or school hours), `tasks` have a day but no clock time, `skipped` is what your assistant saw and left out (and why), `review` is its summary so you can check the list is complete.
Ask your assistant for yours, paste or upload it here, then Apply.
